text:
maya: Quick perf follow-up from the 8xA100 TP+PP run — default kernel selection + dynamic batching. Profiling shows an unexpected all-reduce spike that dominates tail latency.

eric: can you paste the perf summary and the machine topology?

maya: sure, short paste from nvprof/NCCL timeline: 
```
Step time: 210ms
compute: 140ms (66.7%)
all-reduce: 42ms (20%)
host<->dev copies: 10ms (4.8%)
kv-merge/serialization: 18ms (8.6%)
```
machines: 2 nodes x 4xA100 each; intra-node NVLink disabled on this queue so intra-node mostly PCIe peer-to-peer, inter-node via EFA/NCCL over IB.

jenny: ugh, NVLink disabled? that will blow up P2P perf. is NCCL picking a bad ring/graph?

maya: looks like it. NCCL rank ordering ended up pairing GPUs across the PCIe fabric rather than grouping NVLink neighbors. Timeline shows some pairs using PCIe->IB paths instead of NVLink.

eric: can you try topology-aware grouping (group ranks by NVLink cliques) and re-run a single-step benchmark? NCCL provides topology hints if you set ranks appropriately.

maya: did that as an A/B: default vs topo-group. Results: default step 210ms vs topo-group step 192ms. All-reduce dropped from 42ms -> 24ms after grouping (so ~18ms improvement). compute unchanged.

noah: nice. How about comm/compute overlap? are we blocking on reductions before next compute chunk?

maya: yes — kernel selector currently optimizes for peak compute kernels (flash_attn preferred) but ignores an overlap score. With the current scheduling we wait for full tensor chunks before issuing all-reduce; that serializes comm and compute.

eric: we should add a comm-compute overlap metric to the kernel selector. At least prefer split points that let us launch local compute for the next micro-batch while previous micro-batch is doing all-reduce.

maya: agreed. Also saw KV cache merge cost when pipeline stages cross hosts. KV merge/serialization was 18ms; after switching to per-shard lazy merge it went down to ~4ms in follow-up runs. The expensive part was memcpy + protobuf packing on CPU.

jenny: oh that explains some tail latency jitter. Is KV copying happening on the host for EFA path?

maya: yes — inter-node path forces host staging when using our current NIC settings. EFA reduces raw AR latency, but host copy overhead eats some of that win. For EFA runs where NVLink existed intra-node, overall AR% was lower (around 9-12%) but host-copy was still visible if KV shards cross nodes.

maya: quick config snippet I used for the topo-aware run + kernel tweaks: 
```
kernel_selection:
  prefer_fp16: true
  tuned_kernels: ["flash_attn", "cutlass_fused_mlp"]
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  batching_mode: "latency-aware"
kv_cache:
  shard_strategy: "per-pipeline-stage"
  lazy_merge_threshold_ms: 5
```

eric: can you open a perf ticket and include the raw NCCL topo dump + timeline? we need to track two parallel fixes: (1) force topology-aware rank assignment on the scheduler, (2) add overlap-aware kernel selection.

maya: will do. Plan: run 10 trials each for NVLink-enabled, PCIe-only, and EFA/IB setups. Collect: step time, all-reduce median/p90, host-copy times, kv-serialization times, and compute utilization. Then update kernel selector to include an overlap score and evaluate.

jenny: maybe also try disabling dynamic batching tail growth. dynamic batching gave slightly better throughput but increased p99; fixed micro-batches per device with small batching windows might be better for latency SLOs.

noah: agreed — also let's add a micro-benchmark that isolates NCCL all-reduce with our tensor sizes so infra can validate hw topology mapping. I'll queue on perf-nvlink.

maya: thanks — I'll attach the experiments and a short doc with recommended defaults (topo-aware ranks, per-stage KV shards, lazy merges, overlap-aware kernel scoring).

infra-bot: perf run scheduled: perf-nvlink/2026-03-19-01 queued (owner: noah)

jenny: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maya: final note — this explains last week's regression: we changed default rank assignment for simpler placement, but it inadvertently broke NVLink locality on some instance types. I'm reverting that patch and will land the overlap-aware selector in a follow-up PR.
